The certificates were handed over to the Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation and a bamboo farmer from Odisha. Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme The Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme was launched in December 2023 by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. The scheme is branded as PRAMAAN, which is used for certification of forest and wood-based value chains in India. PRAMAAN is linked with sustainable forest management, agroforestry, and responsible practices in wood-based industries. The scheme is also aligned with the National Working Plan Code 2023 and international market requirements such as the European Union Deforestation Regulation. Types of Certification under PRAMAAN The scheme provides three certification categories. Forest Management Certification applies to forests and plantations managed under approved standards. Trees Outside Forests Management Certification applies to trees grown outside recorded forest areas, including farm forestry and agroforestry systems. Chain of Custody Management Certification applies to tracking certified material through processing and trade. Andhra Pradesh is set to become the first state to receive PRAMAAN certification for environmentally sustainable cultivation practices. The certification process covered about 33,000 hectares

bihar_raw_news.content: English News National Flood Alert: 8 Rivers In Spate In UP, Bihar Schools Closed | Latest News Chhattisgarh’s Indravati river breaks 53-year water-level record: Rajasthan hit by hail, UP blanketed by winter-like fog New Delhi 4 hours ago Copy link The water level of the Indravati River in Chhattisgarh’s Bastar district rose to 12.39 metres after heavy rainfall triggered by Cyclone Arnab, breaking a 53-year-old record. The river level surpassed the previous record of 12.18 metres, recorded on July 9, 1973, by 21 cm. Several low-lying areas of Jagdalpur have been inundated, with drone visuals showing extensive flooding in residential areas. Authorities launched rescue operations as the water level continued to rise. On Monday, 833 people were evacuated to safer locations. As many as 65 relief camps have been set up across the district, where 8,894 flood-affected people are currently staying. Rajasthan sees rain, hail as western disturbance brings weather change Several parts of Rajasthan, including Jaipur, Bikaner and Churu, received rain accompanied by hail due to the impact of a western disturbance. The sudden change in weather brought cooler nights, with the minimum temperature in the Shekhawati region falling below 20°C. The weather department has forecast a rise of 3–4°C in temperatures over the next two to three days. Dense fog blankets parts of UP in September Parts of Uttar Pradesh witnessed dense fog on Tuesday morning, with Amethi, Rampur and Badaun reporting significantly reduced visibility. Visibility dropped to around 25 metres in some areas, while residents also experienced a slight chill. The September fog comes as the southwest monsoon has begun withdrawing from the state. The monsoon has already retreated from parts of western Uttar Pradesh, including Muzaffarnagar and Aligarh. With its withdrawal, heavy rainfall has subsided across the state. See the position of monsoon clouds on the satellite map Weather pictures from across the country A mud house collapsed in Bagaha, Bihar, due to strong winds and rain. A 70-year-old, two-storey mansion in Badaun, Uttar Pradesh, collapsed in just 3 seconds. Villagers carry a sick man across a river in Maingadhi, Korba district, Chhattisgarh. Darkness descended on Jaipur from the evening onwards. Heavy rain and strong winds caused considerable inconvenience to people. A landslide occurred near Jangalikh Bridge in Himachal Pradesh's Shimla district on Monday. Mountaineers stranded amid snowfall in Uttarakhand's Uttarkashi were taken to safe locations. . national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah today inaugurated the Conference on ‘PRAHAAR – National CT Policy and Strategy’ in New Delhi. The Conference deliberated upon the seven pillars of PRAHAAR including Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating Conditions for Terrorism, Aligning International Efforts and Recovery and Resilience through a whole-of-society approach. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Shah said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Government has adopted a ‘zero-tolerance’ policy against all forms and manifestations of terrorism. He highlighted that from 2019 to 2026, the Narendra Modi government successfully brought back 288 fugitive criminals to India from 36 countries. Mr Shah said, as a result of better coordination among agencies, more than 40 modules of Shahzad Bhatti network involved in cross-border smuggling of weapons, explosives and narcotics were busted, more than 100 FIRs were registered and 350 individuals were arrested across 15 states. He said, at the same time, the government declared Shahzad Bhatti network a terrorist organisation under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act – UAPA. The Home Minister also stressed on the need for consistent efforts to strengthen and improvise the PRAHAAR strategy through a continuous analysis of terror incidents and establishing a strong and concrete PRAHAAR mechanism for the next 10 years. Focusing on percolation of the tenets of PRAHAAR up to the Thana level, Mr Shah emphasized adopting a proactive approach towards every aspect of the PRAHAAR initiative. Underlining various steps undertaken for mitigating terrorist threats, the Minister advocated institutionalising an automated counter terrorism response at every level of the framework. Mr Shah also called for coordination among the stakeholders to prevent any delay in action and impressed upon the necessity of result-oriented approach towards each pillar of PRAHAAR. Mr Shah also launched a new Extradition Portal, which will synergise and expedite the efforts to bring back fugitives from abroad. He exhorted the State Police Forces to establish dedicated teams for working in tandem with the Central agencies to bring back fugitives from abroad.
